title: Convergent Private Packaging: FlexBand license bands, tiered Ops SLA, and controlled upgrade cadence experiment
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: Redwood Private (VPC / on-prem) sales conversations repeatedly surface two interrelated commercial asks: clearer license sizing that tolerates burst and short-term growth, and predictable operational entitlements (SLA, hotfix response, upgrade windows). Procurement teams also require explicit upgrade and security-patch commitments to align maintenance cycles. Problem: existing flat seat/commit buckets create negotiation friction and unclear answers on security questionnaires. Objective: design and pilot a FlexBand packaging construct pairing flexible license bands, two ops SLA tiers, and selectable upgrade cadences to reduce friction and provide explicit security questionnaire language.
proposal: High-level proposal: 1) FlexBand license bands: monthly license bands mapped to committed inference-units/GPU-hours. Bands: conservatively-sized (Band A), flexible (Band B), and burst-capable (Band C). Include one monthly burst buffer and an overage rate. 2) Ops SLA tiers: Standard (business-hours support; 24h security patch window) and Priority (24x7; 8h security patch window; faster P1 handling). 3) Upgrade cadence choices: Managed Quarterly (Redwood schedules non-breaking upgrades quarterly), Customer-Controlled (customer schedules certified upgrade packages within 90-day security window), and Airgap/Locked (only security patches delivered within contracted windows). Commercial plumbing: base band price + ops-tier surcharge +/- upgrade cadence uplift or discount; monthly reconciliation of overages with transparent reporting.
experiment_plan: Define three pilot offers aligned to Band A/B/C with explicit pricing, burst allowances, and an offer variant for regulated verticals.
Recruit six inbound deals (target ARR > $150k) over 8 weeks via Sales Ops; include at least two regulated/financial customers.
Prepare standardized contract language, SOW inserts, and security questionnaire snippets; secure Legal pre-approval prior to outreach.
Instrument deal desk: capture time-to-sign, redline cycles, number of security-Q follow-ups, and support cost commitments.
Run Finance run-rate projections and Engineering capacity simulations for sustained and worst-case burst scenarios.
Conduct post-sign interviews and collect security-team questionnaire completion time and blocking issues.
success_metrics: Reduce average time-to-sign for pilot deals by >=25% vs historical baseline for deals >$150k.
Increase win rate on on-prem/VPC proposals from ~18% baseline to >=30% within pilot cohort.
Achieve <=2 contract redline cycles for >=70% of pilot deals using pre-approved language.
Engineering impact: sustained capacity increase <2% and burst allowance covered by pooled safety buffer in >=90% of pilot months.
Security questionnaire turnaround time reduced by >=40% due to templated upgrade commitments.
